subject: Post-call: burst token pool & connection pooling — next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@elliott-systems.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@elliott-systems.com
Date: 2028-06-30T15:10:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Concurrency & burst needs (Elliott)

Dylan — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side so everyone is aligned:

- SLA targets: p95 generation latency target <= 250ms for standard requests; for streaming chat we want chunking latency <= 100ms.
- Concurrency: sustained ~400 parallel requests across our US region during business hours, with the ability to burst to ~2,000 parallel in a 90–120s window for marketing spikes.
- Connections: our frontend uses long-lived WebSocket streams and we prefer multiplexing many logical sessions over a small number of TCP/TLS sockets (connection pool per edge node).
- Throughput: typical token rate is ~50 tokens/sec per user during a conversation, average session length 80 tokens. Peak QPS estimate ~1,400 requests/sec during burst.

Ask: can Redwood support a token-bucket or burst token mechanism that lets us temporarily exceed baseline quotas without service interruption? Also need an initial sense of rate limits, pricing for burst capacity, and any changes required to our client to support recommended pooling.

Attached: a short diagram of our streaming topology and an internal SOW draft.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Integrations, Elliott Systems
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@elliott-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Concurrency & burst needs (Elliott)

Samantha — really helpful recap, thanks. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

Summary of what Redwood can offer for a fast trial:
- Baseline quota: we can provision a sustained concurrency allowance of 500 parallel requests for your US region on a Hosted Dedicated plan.
- Burst token bucket: we have a configurable burst-token mechanism (server-side token bucket) that can allow temporary bursts up to 2000 parallel requests for up to 2 minutes. Tokens refill at a configurable rate.
- Connection pooling: our recommended pattern is multiplexing logical sessions over 8–16 persistent sockets per app instance. That minimizes TLS handshakes while keeping per-GPU session overhead low.
- Streaming: our websocket streaming path supports sub-100ms chunk latency in most regions; we'll need to confirm with a short synthetic test against your client.

Pricing/limits: provisional numbers attached in redwood-ratecard-v3.pdf. For the trial we can waive the burst surcharge for the first 2 weeks so you can validate traffic patterns.

Engineering questions for sizing: can you confirm active edge nodes (how many app instances/pool members) and whether bursts are global or concentrat ed to a single region? Also: do you have sticky routing (same user -> same edge) or stateless LB?

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood inflight: Ben to validate the token-bucket params and supply a draft config for your infra (Ben). [ETA: 2028-07-01]
- Redwood ops: Marissa will enable a temporary trial quota and coordinate observability hooks (Marissa). [ETA: 2028-07-02]
- Customer: Samantha to confirm number of edge nodes and whether bursts are per-region or global.

If that sounds right I can open an interim HubSpot deal and send a trial PO link.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha@elliott-systems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T02:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: Concurrency config & token-bucket draft

Forwarding a quick engineering note and draft config. Attachment: connpool-diagram.png (stub).

On our side, a few concrete numbers that should map to your traffic profile:
- Sustained concurrency 500 => estimate ~0.4 GPU cores of sustained served KV/cache per 256-token window per replica; we'll size autoscale to keep p95 latency under 250ms.
- Burst: token-bucket with capacity 2,000 tokens, refill rate 50 tokens/sec. That yields a ~40s effective sustained above-baseline before refill stabilizes; we can tune refill up if your expected burst window is 90–120s.
- Fairness: we recommend a per-customer SLA token queue to avoid noisy-neighbor impact; during bursts non-critical background jobs should be deprioritized.

Client-side recommendations:
- Maintain 8 persistent sockets per instance and multiplex up to 100 logical sessions per socket. This aligns with our internal connection pooling heuristics.
- Implement exponential backoff for 429s with jitter. We'll provide a test endpoint that emits realistic 429 traces so you can tune.

I'll attach a config snippet (see connpool-diagram.png) with suggested token counts. Happy to run numbers against your exact session distribution.

—Ben
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@elliott-systems.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@elliott-systems.com
Date: 2028-07-01T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Concurrency config & token-bucket draft

Thanks Ben — that helps a lot. Clarifications: our bursts are typically global (across US edges) but often start concentrated in a few nodes for the first 30–60s. We run roughly 20 app instances per edge PoP today.

We're happy to proceed with the trial if Redwood will:
1) provision the 500 sustained + 2000 burst token bucket for 2 weeks (no burst surcharge)
2) provide the synthetic test endpoint and a short runbook for handling 429s
3) enable tracing headers so we can correlate p95 and token consumption in your console

I've attached a preliminary SOW (SOW-Elliott-Draft.pdf). Procurement is OK to sign a short trial PO once we have the HubSpot record/DocuSign link.

Samantha
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@elliott-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procurement@elliott-systems.com
Date: 2028-07-01T10:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Concurrency config & token-bucket draft — trial activation

Cheers,
Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
